title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: From painting a massive mountain monogram to the thunderous boom of a vintage cannon, Colorado State University's traditions celebrate its deep agricultural roots and spirited Ram family.

cards.title: Painting the A
cards.subtitle: A Century-Old Mountain Makeover
cards.notes: Join hundreds of students each August to whitewash the 450-foot 'A' on the hogback west of campus, a tradition dating back to 1923.
cards.short_summary: An annual event where students hike up the Maxwell Natural Area to repaint the massive 'A' monogram representing the school's Aggie heritage.
cards.evidence_claim: The 'A' was first completed in September 1924 and is 450 feet tall; students continue to paint it annually in August.
cards.source_title: A 100-year old tradition | STATE - The Magazine of the Colorado State University System
cards.access_notes: The site is located in the Maxwell Natural Area; the painting event is organized by the Alumni Association.

cards.title: Firing Comatose
cards.subtitle: The Loudest Game Day Ritual
cards.notes: Listen for the thunderous boom of this 1918 French 75mm field gun, fired by Army ROTC cadets every time the Rams score a touchdown.
cards.short_summary: A vintage cannon named 'Comatose' that has been a fixture of CSU football games since 1920, signaling scores and kickoffs.
cards.evidence_claim: The tradition of firing a cannon during football games started in 1920; it is currently managed by Army ROTC cadets.
cards.access_notes: Fired at Canvas Stadium during home football games.

cards.title: CAM the Ram's Sprint
cards.subtitle: The Official Animal Ambassador
cards.notes: Watch CAM the Ram and his student handlers sprint across the end zone during home games, a tradition since the mascot's naming in 1954.
cards.short_summary: The live Rambouillet ram mascot who leads the team onto the field and celebrates touchdowns with a spirited run.
cards.evidence_claim: CAM was officially named in 1954; student volunteers known as Ram Handlers manage his care and game-day sprints.
cards.source_title: CAM the Ram - CSU Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: Appears at Canvas Stadium and various campus events; managed by the Alumni Association.

cards.title: Ringing the Old Main Bell
cards.subtitle: A Returned Historic Treasure
cards.notes: Celebrate Ram victories by ringing this 500-pound bell, which was stolen in 1919 and mysteriously returned to campus in 2016.
cards.short_summary: A historic bell from the original Old Main building that is now rung to signify football wins and other major university triumphs.
cards.evidence_claim: The bell was manufactured in 1894, stolen around 1919, and returned anonymously in 2016; it now hangs in the Alumni Center tower.
cards.source_title: The Old Main Bell: Historic treasure returns to campus
cards.access_notes: Located at the Iris & Michael Smith Alumni Center; rung during special events and after victories.

cards.title: The Bronze Boot Run
cards.subtitle: Border War Rivalry Ritual
cards.notes: Witness ROTC cadets relay the game ball 65 miles along Highway 287 between Fort Collins and Laramie before the annual Border War game.
cards.short_summary: A pre-game tradition where CSU and Wyoming ROTC cadets run the game ball to the state line to compete for a bronzed Vietnam combat boot.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bronze Boot is a combat boot worn in Vietnam by Capt. Dan Romero; the relay run along U.S. 287 has been a ritual since the late 1960s.
cards.source_title: Bronze Boot Run - Colorado State University
cards.access_notes: The run occurs on the Friday before the CSU vs. Wyoming football game.

cards.title: Nutrien Ag Day BBQ
cards.subtitle: Honoring Agricultural Roots
cards.notes: Feast on Colorado-grown food at this massive pre-game barbecue that has celebrated CSU's land-grant mission for over 40 years.
cards.short_summary: An annual celebration of Colorado agriculture featuring a large public BBQ and the football team wearing 'Aggie Orange' uniforms.
cards.evidence_claim: Ag Day has been a tradition for over 40 years; the event includes a BBQ showcasing Colorado commodities and orange throwback uniforms.
cards.access_notes: Held annually at the Ag Day BBQ site near Canvas Stadium; tickets required for the meal.

cards.title: Grill the Buffs
cards.subtitle: The Ultimate Rivalry Pep Rally
cards.notes: Eat a free burger and get hyped for the Rocky Mountain Showdown at this annual pep rally held on the Lory Student Center lawn.
cards.short_summary: A student-led tradition where thousands of free burgers are grilled to build spirit before the game against the CU Buffaloes.
cards.evidence_claim: The 14th annual Grill the Buffs was held in 2023; it is hosted by the Associated Students of CSU (ASCSU) and features free burgers.
cards.source_title: Colorado State celebrates 14th annual Grill the Buffs
cards.access_notes: Held on the Lory Student Center West Lawn during the week of the CU game.

cards.title: I Love CSU Day
cards.subtitle: A Statewide Proclamation of Pride
cards.notes: Wear green and gold every April 18th to celebrate this official Colorado holiday dedicated to Ram pride and community spirit.
cards.short_summary: A university-wide day of pride featuring on-campus festivities, tie-dye stations, and social media celebrations.
cards.evidence_claim: I Love CSU Day is observed annually on April 18 by official governor proclamation; events include tie-dyeing and campus scavenger hunts.
cards.source_title: I Love CSU Day - CSU Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: Celebrated across campus and online; primary hub is the Smith Alumni Center.

cards.title: Friday Night Lights Bonfire
cards.subtitle: Homecoming's Blazing Centerpiece
cards.notes: Gather on the LSC West Lawn for a massive bonfire, fireworks, and the lighting of the 'A' during Homecoming weekend.
cards.short_summary: A historic Homecoming tradition featuring a large community bonfire and pep rally to welcome alumni back to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The bonfire tradition dates back to at least 1910; it is currently part of the 'Friday Night Lights' event during Homecoming.
cards.source_title: Friday Night Lights – CSU Homecoming & Family Weekend
cards.access_notes: Held on the lawn west of the Lory Student Center; free and open to the public.

cards.title: Walking the Oval
cards.subtitle: The Heart of Campus
cards.notes: Stroll beneath the century-old American Elms in this historic heart of campus, a site for graduations and quiet reflection since 1909.
cards.short_summary: The iconic, elm-lined green space that serves as the symbolic center of the university and the site of major ceremonial traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Oval was designed in 1909 and features 93 American Elms, some dating back to the 1880s; it is the primary site for graduation celebrations.
cards.source_title: The Oval: Preserving a Living Legacy
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible park-like space in the center of campus.
